questions.prompt: The Church distinguishes 'latria,' 'dulia,' and 'hyperdulia.' What does latria mean?
choices: The adoration owed to God alone
Veneration owed to the saints
The special veneration given to Mary
Honor given to sacred images and relics
questions.correctAnswer: The adoration owed to God alone
questions.explanation: Latria is never given to any creature — not to Mary, not to the greatest saint, not to an angel. The whole point of the three-word distinction is to make the line impossible to blur: one word for God alone, and two further words dividing up everything owed to creatures.
questions.hint: This is the only one of the three terms that can never, under any circumstance, apply to a creature.

questions.prompt: 'Hyperdulia' is the term for the veneration given specifically to:
choices: Mary alone, as greater than the veneration given to any other saint
God the Father specifically
Relics of the True Cross
Icons in Eastern liturgy generally
questions.correctAnswer: Mary alone, as greater than the veneration given to any other saint
questions.explanation: Hyperdulia is still dulia — the honor owed to a creature, not adoration — but raised to its highest degree because of who she is in relation to Christ. It is a difference of degree within veneration, never a crossing over into adoration.
questions.hint: The Greek prefix means 'above' or 'beyond' — beyond ordinary dulia, but still short of latria.

questions.prompt: True or False: Because hyperdulia is a greater degree of honor than dulia, it is a step closer to latria and can shade into it under the right circumstances.
questions.explanation: False, and this is the exact misunderstanding the three-term distinction exists to block. Latria differs from dulia and hyperdulia in kind, not in degree — no amount of veneration, however great, becomes adoration. Hyperdulia is the ceiling of dulia, not a floor under latria.
questions.hint: Ask whether the difference between latria and the other two terms is a difference of amount or a difference of kind.

questions.prompt: Scripture mentions 'brothers' of Jesus, including James and Joseph. What is the traditional Catholic response to this, given the dogma of Mary's perpetual virginity?
choices: The Hebrew and Aramaic behind 'brother' covered a wide range of kin, and the same Gospels identify these two as sons of a different Mary
The Church denies these verses are authentic Scripture
The Church teaches Joseph had children from a previous marriage, and this is the only response ever offered
The Church has no response and treats this as an open contradiction
questions.correctAnswer: The Hebrew and Aramaic behind 'brother' covered a wide range of kin, and the same Gospels identify these two as sons of a different Mary
questions.explanation: Matthew's own Gospel names 'Mary the mother of James and Joseph' as a distinct woman present at the crucifixion — not the mother of Jesus. Hebrew and Aramaic had no separate word for 'cousin' or 'kinsman'; 'ah' (and the Greek 'adelphos' used to translate it) regularly covered brothers, cousins, and other close relatives, as it does in the Septuagint's own use of the same word for Lot, Abraham's nephew.
questions.hint: Compare Matthew 27:56 to Matthew 13:55 and ask whose sons James and Joseph actually are.

citations.quote: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
Let there be no strife between you and me... for we are kinsmen.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Gospels name the 'brothers of the Lord' as James and Joseph without ever separately identifying a mother named Mary who is distinct from Jesus' mother.
questions.explanation: False. Matthew 27:56 and Mark 15:40 both explicitly name 'Mary the mother of James and Joseph/Joses' as a woman present at the crucifixion, standing alongside Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Jesus is not listed as her — the traditional identification of this second Mary is the wife of Clopas from John 19:25.
questions.hint: Check whether the Gospels actually name a second Mary as the mother of James and Joseph.

citations.quote: standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother... and Mary the wife of Clopas

questions.prompt: An objection runs: 'If Mary is called Mediatrix, doesn't that make her a second mediator alongside Christ, contradicting 1 Timothy 2:5?' What is the accurate Catholic response?
choices: Her mediation is entirely derivative, flowing from and dependent on Christ's one mediation, never alongside or independent of it
1 Timothy 2:5 has been formally reinterpreted by the Church and no longer applies
There are in fact two equal mediators, and the objection correctly identifies a real tension
The title Mediatrix was withdrawn after Vatican II
questions.correctAnswer: Her mediation is entirely derivative, flowing from and dependent on Christ's one mediation, never alongside or independent of it
questions.explanation: Lumen Gentium answers this directly: her role 'flows forth from the superabundance of the merits of Christ' and depends entirely on it — the same relationship a beam of light has to its source, not two separate lights. Paul's 'one mediator' and Mary's intercession are not in competition because her intercession is not a second, independent channel.
questions.hint: Ask whether her mediation is presented as a second source alongside Christ's, or as something running through his.

citations.quote: For there is one God. There is also one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
the maternal duty of Mary toward men in no way obscures or diminishes this unique mediation of Christ, but rather shows its power.

questions.prompt: The Council of Ephesus's condemnation of Nestorius is sometimes mistaken for elevating Mary above her actual role. What did Ephesus actually intend to protect?
choices: The unity of Christ's person — that one and the same Son is both God and man
Mary's own sinlessness
The primacy of the Bishop of Rome
The canon of Scripture
questions.correctAnswer: The unity of Christ's person — that one and the same Son is both God and man
questions.explanation: This is worth restating precisely because the objection recurs: Ephesus is a Christological council that uses a Marian title as its instrument. Get the title wrong, and you have actually gotten Christ wrong — split him into two persons rather than exalted his mother.
questions.hint: Ask what the council was actually trying to settle, using Mary's title as the test case.

questions.prompt: St. Jerome's fourth-century treatise responding to the claim that Mary had other children by Joseph is titled Against ____.
questions.explanation: Helvidius argued from the 'brothers of the Lord' passages that Mary bore other children after Jesus. Jerome's rebuttal — arguing from the same linguistic point about Hebrew and Aramaic kinship terms used in level nine's earlier question — became the standard patristic answer, still used today.
questions.hint: The title is simply 'Against' the name of the man Jerome is refuting.

citations.quote: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

questions.prompt: True or False: Because Mary's title 'Mother of God' answers a fifth-century Christological dispute, it has no bearing on ordinary Catholic devotion today.
questions.explanation: False. The title is prayed daily in the Hail Mary and in the Church's liturgy precisely because the doctrine it defends — who Christ really is — remains true every day, not only in the fifth century. A dogma settled once does not become inert; it keeps doing its work every time it is prayed.
questions.hint: Ask whether a settled dogma stops mattering once the historical controversy that produced it has ended.
